strategies.overview: Deoxys-D's access to the highly coveted Teleport is complemented by its excellent supportive movepool and high defenses. This gives it a niche in being a slow pivot that can take a strong hit and safely bring in another teammate to threaten the opposing team, often creating setup opportunities. Additionally, it's a great physically defensive blanket check for offensive teams that lack a defensive backbone to fall back on. Deoxys-D has a wide utility movepool that can benefit more defensive teams as well, since it has access to moves such as Knock Off, Taunt, Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Thunder Wave, all of which help it make progress against slower teams. Deoxys-D also removes items quite easily, inviting in Pokemon such as Bisharp, Registeel, and Golurk, none of which appreciate Knock Off. However, Deoxys-D has many flaws that prevent it from being common. It has a bad defensive typing that leaves it vulnerable to common Pokemon like Krookodile, Bisharp and Gengar as well as the ubiquitous U-turn from the likes of Galarian Zapdos and Jirachi, which can lead to it being overwhelmed by the very Pokemon it's supposed to check. Furthermore, it's very weak and passive, making it easy setup fodder for the likes of Reuniclus and Armarouge. Deoxys-D suffers from four-moveslot syndrome, forcing it to choose between being able to disrupt its foes or making long-term progress with Spikes. Finally, Deoxys-D faces strong competition from Pokemon such as Jirachi, Slowbro, Gligar, and Klefki, all of which can either pivot, set entry hazards, or wall Pokemon more effectively.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Leftovers is an alternative if running Spikes in conjunction with Cyclizar, simultaneously lessening pressure to constantly use Recover and making it easier to set multiple layers of Spikes. Rocky Helmet punishes Maushold and prevents Jirachi from trying to flinch Deoxys-D until it gets KOed. Tera Steel gives it a Flying and Bug resistance and much more valuable defensive typing, though it makes it weaker to wallbreakers like Mamoswine. Future Sight could be used to force switches with Teleport to maneuver into an advantageous situation, but it is often too weak. Night Shade gives Deoxys-D consistent, if middling, damage. Mental Herb can negate Taunt from the likes of Krookodile and Noivern once, but other items are more consistent. Deoxys-D can sweep with a moveset of Cosmic Power / Stored Power / Recover / Night Shade, but it often gets overwhelmed and hates the prevalence of Dark-types.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-types like Bisharp, Krookodile, and Crawdaunt can switch into anything Deoxys-D can throw at them and set up or threaten it out with super effective STAB attacks. However, they usually don't appreciate Knock Off, and some cannot break through Deoxys-D if it's running Colbur Berry.

Setup Sweepers: Slow setup sweepers like Reuniclus and Registeel can use Deoxys-D as setup fodder unless it's running Taunt. Similarly, non-Thunder Wave variants will let faster sweepers like Armarouge and Gyarados set up with impunity.

Ghost-types*: Gengar can potentially set up against or irreparably damage Deoxys-D. Basculegion-F and Golurk can switch into Deoxys-D and threaten it out easily; Golurk can even block its Thunder Wave. None of these Pokemon like to take a Knock Off, though, and Gengar and Basculegion-F must be wary of paralysis.

Chip Damage: Entry hazards can wear down Deoxys-D easily throughout the match, forcing it to waste turns using Recover. Deoxys-D has a tendency to lose its item because it's often a switch-in to Pokemon like Galarian Zapdos and Mamoswine, and this can make entry hazards problematic. Similarly, although Deoxys-D checks Pokemon like Galarian Zapdos, Jirachi, and Barraskewda, if they click U-turn or Flip Turn, it will cause a lot of chip damage, which can compromise Deoxys-D's ability to pivot effectively.

movesets.name: Utility
movesets.description:
Set Details

Deoxys-D has many viable options for moves, and it's possible to mix and match any combination if it might fit its team better. Teleport supports its teammates with slow pivoting. Knock Off is an excellent support move and synergizes well with the entry hazards that Deoxys-D sets, helping wear down Pokemon like Cyclizar, Bisharp, and Talonflame while hitting Gengar and Basculegion-F. Thunder Wave helps prevent it from being setup fodder against Pokemon like Armarouge, Gengar, and Gyarados. Psychic Noise can hit Pokemon like Galarian Zapdos, Amoonguss, and Terrakion. Taunt can be very useful in preventing Deoxys-D from getting statused, hazards being laid, and slow setup sweepers like Slowbro and Suicune from setting up on its face. For both Taunt and Psychic Noise, preventing walls like Empoleon and Hippowdon from healing can put pressure on the opposing team in tandem with Teleport safely letting in wallbreakers. Spikes is preferred because Deoxys-D can set up multiple layers to pressure the opposing team, though Stealth Rock should be used instead if it cannot be fit somewhere else on the team. Heavy-Duty Boots helps with pivoting by minimizing chip damage. Colbur Berry improves its matchup against Knock Off users such as Galarian Zapdos, Krookodile, and Mamoswine and is particularly useful on offense teams where switching into these threats can be very hard otherwise. 16 Speed EVs let Deoxys-D outspeed offensive Hisuian Goodra and Magnezone and use Knock Off before they can attack. The rest is dumped into Defense to switch into Galarian Zapdos and Mamoswine better. Since Deoxys-D often forgoes special attacks, an Impish nature maximizes Knock Off damage, but a Bold nature should be run if using Psychic Noise instead. If Deoxys-D eschews attacking moves altogether, then Bold is superior because it is better into Foul Play. A specially defensive spread is a viable alternative if running Deoxys-D with other physical walls like Hippowdon, Klefki, and Wo-Chien, letting it switch into Pokemon like Armarouge and Volcanion and cripple them or pivot out; 96 Speed EVs let it outspeed Volcanion. Pressure lessens the chance of Jirachi flinching Deoxys-D down and drains low PP moves such as Entei's Sacred Fire and Volcanion's Steam Eruption. Tera Ghost lets Deoxys-D spinblock Cyclizar, ensuring its hazards stay up; counter Maushold; and gain a useful Bug resistance, aiding it against U-turn. If the team already has a spinblocker or keeping Spikes on the field isn't central to the team's gameplan, other Tera types can be useful as well; Tera Fairy gives Deoxys-D a better defensive typing that allows it switch into Pokemon like Galarian Zapdos, Krookodile, and Mienshao more consistently, while Tera Water completely walls Volcanion and helps against Pokemon like Barraskewda and Bisharp. Both Tera types also get rid of Deoxys-D's Bug and Ghost weaknesses.

Deoxys-D is an excellent support Pokemon on offensive structures because it provides a defensive blanket check and can easily pivot into more threatening teammates with Teleport; most of the tier's offensive Pokemon appreciate getting in safely. Deoxys-D is also a decent option on balance teams, where it can make consistent progress with its various utility moves. Slow or frail wallbreakers such as Mamoswine, Volcanion, and Gallade can use slow pivot support to safely break holes into the opposing team early in the game. The holes opened up by them can then be exploited later on by sweepers and cleaners such as Maushold and Galarian Zapdos. In return, Deoxys-D can help pave the way for a sweep with its utility moves and pivoting support. If Deoxys-D is running a set without Thunder Wave, setup sweepers like Armarouge and Gyarados can easily take advantage of it. Therefore, priority users like Mimikyu, Entei, Bisharp, and Mamowsine can help alleviate this concern. Cyclizar complements Spikes Deoxys-D quite well, since Rapid Spin doesn't remove entry hazards on the opposing side unlike Defog Talonflame and Noivern. On top of that, it checks problematic Ghost-types like Basculegion-F and Gengar for Deoxys-D; Krookodile can do the same and also set Stealth Rock. Since Deoxys-D can struggle against VoltTurn, Pokemon like Talonflame and Hippowdon can discourage the use of U-turn and Volt Switch on more defensive builds. Checks to Dark-types, like Galarian Zapdos, Mienshao, and Chensaught are necessary to deal with Bisharp and Krookodile. Galarian Zapdos and Mienshao can form a pivoting core with Deoxys-D while both offering Knock Off. Stealth Rock setters like Terrakion, Krookodile, and Hippowdon let Deoxys-D run Spikes and can form a hazard stacking core with it. On Spikes stacking teams, additional Knock Off support from the likes of Krookodile and Wo-Chien is useful to remove Heavy-Duty Boots, and pivoting cores that threaten each other's checks, such as Galarian Zapdos and Basculegion-F or Mienshao and Choice Specs Magnezone, can maximize chip damage quickly by repeatedly threatening out foes.

strategies.overview:
Psychic

Deoxys-D is outclassed as a stallbreaker by other Psychic-types such as Gallade and Hoopa-U that can provide the team with more offensive pressure. With its stallbreaking capabilities, its best suited for more passive teams such as Flying. The trait that Deoxys-D provides is Pressure stalling foes out while wearing down their HP with Night Shade and making use of Recover to shrug off damage after boosting its stats with Cosmic Power. Physically defensive Deoxys-D has competition from teammates like Slowbro, as it offers Regenerator and Scald; however, Deoxys-D has a more utility-condensed moveset notably consisting of Teleport and Spikes and takes on foes like the Ogerpon formes. Using this forme also restricts usage of Deoxys-S, a desirable wallbreaker and revenge killer that has access to the same utility moves, albeit it's more frail.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Psychic

Stallbreaker Deoxys-D can alternatively run Stored Power, becoming a threat if there are no Dark-types on the field. Covert Cloak can be run to cancel out secondary effects. Physically defensive Deoxys-D may opt for Rocky Helmet allowing for passive chip damage alongside Spikes, punishing multi-hit moves like Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and pivot moves such as U-turn from Cinderace and Landorus-T, as well as Flip Turn from Barraskewda.

movesets.name: Stallbreaker (Psychic)
movesets.description:
With its phenomenal defenses, Deoxys-D can make a great impact for Psychic teams as a stallbreaker that takes advantage of more passive teams such as Flying. Cosmic Power makes it able to handle wallbreakers and Choice-locked Pokemon. With 176 Speed EVs, Deoxys-D is able to outspeed and use Cosmic Power against Choice Band Dragonite and Mamoswine and most Gliscor sets, allowing Deoxys-D to block its entry hazards and Toxic with Taunt. Taunt also stops walls such as Blissey, Skarmory, and Toxapex from spreading status and setting hazards while limiting their longevity. Night Shade is Deoxys-D's most consistent form of damage dealing.

Gallade is a powerful secondary wallbreaker in conjunction with Deoxys-D, making use of its Fighting-type STAB attacks to remove Dark-type threats that Deoxys-D can't handle on its own such as Ting-Lu, Alolan Muk, and Greninja. Espathra can set up once Deoxys-D removes walls. Hoopa-U complements. Deoxys-D as a threat to Ghost-types such as Gholdengo and Flutter Mane. Iron Boulder, with its phenomenal Speed, can pair greatly with Deoxys-D to remove Dark-, Bug-, and Fire-type threats such as Meowscarada, Volcarona, and Ogerpon-H. Choice Specs Latios appreciates Deoxys-D stalling out special walls such as Hisuian Goodra and Ting-Lu and, in return, handles threats such as Hydreigon. Hatterene provides entry hazard control in case Deoxys-Dis not able to outspeed and use Taunt while also providing great bulk and Fairy-type coverage to deal with Dragon-types such as Garchomp and Kyurem. Jirachi can pair excellently with Deoxys-D to be not only a defensive pair but also a Stealth Rock setter. Alternatively, Metagross can set Stealth Rock while also posing a threat to Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Mimikyu.

movesets.name: Physically Defensive
movesets.description:
Deoxys-D boasts impeccable defensive stats and a wide range of utility moves, benefiting Psychic as a bulky pivot and entry hazard setter. Night Shade prevents Deoxys-D from being too passive and deals decent chunks of damage over time. Alternatively, Knock Off may be used to accentuate Spikes usage by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Toxapex and Sableye, forcing progress and easing the jobs of wallbreaker teammates. Teleport allows for slow and safe pivoting for offensive teammates such as Iron Boulder, Indeedee-M, and Latios, while Taunt prevents opposing defensive Pokemon like Archaludon and Mandibuzz from setting up Stealth Rock and using Toxic, respectively. Spikes wears down threatening foes such as Flutter Mane, Greninja, and Ogerpon-H, building up passive damage alongside Night Shade. Thunder Wave may also be used to paralyze quicker targets such as Ogerpon formes with Horn Leech, which can negate Night Shade damage, Roaring Moon, and Greninja. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Deoxys-D to repeatedly use Teleport and get swapped in without having to worry about hazards; however, Leftovers may be used to better sponge attacks due to passive recovery.

Hoopa-U is greatly appreciated by Deoxys-D, as it threatens Ghost-type Pokemon like Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Pecharunt. In exchange, Hoopa-U values getting brought in by Teleport and Spikes wearing down switch-ins such as Ting-Lu and Archaludon. Galarian Slowking forms a defensive core with Deoxys-D, taking on special attackers like Latios, Iron Moth, and Primarina, while Deoxys-D walls Iron Treads, Swampert, and Iron Boulder. They also both form a pivot core due to Galarian Slowking's access to Chilly Reception, preserving a lot of momentum for the rest of the team. Hatterene aids in preventing the setting of entry hazards via Magic Bounce while combating Dark-types such as Hydreigon, Darkrai, and Roaring Moon. Iron Boulder pressures offensive threats like Volcarona, Weavile, and Tornadus-T, valuing Spikes and Teleport support in return. Latios appreciates Deoxys-D setting up Spikes and providing slow pivoting with Teleport while Latios pressures Dragon teams, notably removing Hydreigon. Choice Scarf Indeedee-M picks off wallbreakers such as Swords Dance Urshifu-R and Sneasler while also providing a Ghost-type immunity and Healing Wish support should Deoxys-D get low on health or inflicted by a status. Metagross contributes to the hazard stack via Stealth Rock and pressures faster threats such as Flutter Mane and Weavile with Bullet Punch.

strategies.outdated: This analysis is from before our transition to full analyses, and may contain outdated information.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description: Boasting high defensive stats and a plethora of utility moves, Deoxys-D makes for an excellent Unaware wall that can check Iron Hands and setup Great Tusk while also providing additional utility like setting entry hazards and pivoting. Spikes is the preferred hazard, as Deoxys-D can usually set multiple layers, but Stealth Rock is an alternative for teams that lack a Stealth Rock setter otherwise, and Knock Off can be used to limit opposing setup threats like Iron Boulder and Quaquaval while also debilitating walls like Corviknight and Swampert. Teleport can be used in conjunction with Deoxys-D's low Speed to safely switch Pokemon in, while Thunder Wave can be used to cripple Iron Boulder and Dragonite. Leftovers is the preferred item for extra longevity, but Heavy-Duty Boots is an option on Teleport sets to enable easier pivoting. On teams that do not need setup control, Fluffy and Intimidate dramatically increase its physical bulk versus key targets like Iron Boulder. Defensive Pokemon like Corviknight and Mandibuzz appreciate Deoxys-D being able to take on setup threats such as Iron Hands and Iron Boulder, allowing them to better handle Dark-types like Roaring Moon. Offensive Pokemon like Galarian Zapdos, Chien-Pao, and Ceruledge appreciate Deoxys-D being able to weaken opposing walls with hazards or Knock Off, as well as potentially getting them in safely if it's running Teleport. Deoxys-D narrowly avoids 2HKOs from stronger wallbreakers like Iron Boulder, so hazard control options like Scrappy Great Tusk and Corviknight are highly recommended so that Deoxys-D can have more longevity.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 4 onwards

Price Range: 12-14 points

Overview: Deoxys-D's incredible defenses, movepool, and good Speed tier for a defensive Pokemon allow it to serve as a versatile defensive utility Pokemon. It has access to valuable utility moves such as Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Teleport while also having longevity with Recover to stay healthy enough to wall offensive threats during battle. Alternatively, it can use its natural bulk to find setup opportunities and bolster its lacking offenses to dangerous levels in combination with Stored Power. However, Deoxys-D is held back by a poor defensive typing that lacks many resistances, which makes its bulk less effective in practice than it appears on paper. Terastallization can help it with this issue, but it still struggles to overcome its passivity.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Defensive Wall: Deoxys-D leverages its immense bulk and longevity with Recover to wall offensive threats. These sets tend to lack significant damage output, but they try to make up for it by running moves that are uncomfortable to switch in on like Knock Off and Thunder Wave.

Utility: Deoxys-D can make for a great utility Pokemon. It can fairly reliably set entry hazards or dual screens due to its Speed letting it avoid Taunt from many slower foes and also survive multiple attacks due to its great natural bulk. After it sets up what it wants, it can use Teleport to safely bring in one of its teammates.

Setup Sweeper: Occasionally, Deoxys-D can become a wincon with some combination of its many setup moves. These sets have two main variants: the first focuses on boosting Stored Power as much as possible and usually holds Weakness Policy, while the second focuses on winning via attrition by increasing Deoxys-D's bulk as much as possible and attempts to become impossible to KO without a foe landing a critical hit.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Psychic Noise, Psycho Boost, Psychic, Stored Power, Psyshock

Setup Moves: Agility, Calm Mind, Cosmic Power, Iron Defense, Nasty Plot

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Spikes, Knock Off, Teleport, Taunt, Night Shade, Thunder Wave, Recover, Reflect, Light Screen, Trick, Protect

Coverage: Energy Ball, Focus Blast, Ice Beam, Shadow Ball, Superpower, Thunderbolt

Niche Moves

Trick Room: Deoxys-D is one of the only Pokemon with access to both Trick Room and Teleport, which means it can set Trick Room and then use Teleport to safely bring in a slow offensive threat while maximizing turns of Trick Room support.

Future Sight: Deoxys-D's bulk, ability to slow pivot, and Psychic STAB are all great traits to make Future Sight more useful; its low Special Attack makes Future Sight not as effective as it could be, but it can still be useful sometimes.

Counter / Mirror Coat: Deoxys-D almost always survives any kind of attack if it's healthy enough, so it can make use of Counter or Mirror Coat to surprise KO foes that attempt to break the defensive wall that is Deoxys-D.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: Deoxys-D dislikes all forms of entry hazards, so it commonly uses Heavy-Duty Boots to avoid their residual damage.

Leftovers: When entry hazards aren't as much of a concern, Leftovers gives Deoxys-D passive recovery that all of its sets appreciate.

Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is an alternative to Leftovers for a quick burst of healing, which can be better sometimes.

Niche Items

Weakness Policy: Weakness Policy is only used on offensive setup sweeper Deoxys-D variants, usually in combination with Stored Power.

Mental Herb: Mental Herb can be used on lead Deoxys-D sets to play around faster foes using Taunt.

Light Clay: Light Clay is useful when running dual screens.

Resistance Berries: Deoxys-D's bulk usually lets it survive unboosted super effective attacks, but a resistance Berry can be used to survive a boosted super effective attack or potentially turn a 2HKO into a 3HKO. While it doesn't have the offensive capabilities to take full advantage of this, it can sometimes be useful as an emergency stop to an opposing setup sweeper to hinder them with a move like Thunder Wave.

Tera

Deoxys-D can make great use of Tera, but it is relatively weaker than other potential Tera Captains within its price range. It mostly uses defensive Tera types like Tera Water, Fairy, Poison, and Steel to serve as a better defensive wall or enable its bulky setup sweeper sets. Alternatively, it can use Tera Ghost to spinblock on its entry hazard lead sets or Tera Psychic to boost Stored Power on offensive setup sweeper sets. With all that being said, Deoxys-D's offensive potential takes a lot of setup to get going, so in many matchups, it won't be effective. Tera definitely helps Deoxys-D a lot, but it's hard to justify over other Pokemon that make great defensive and offensive use of Tera more consistently than it does. However, if a team doesn't have better Tera Captain options, Deoxys-D can definitely be a good choice.

Draft Strategy

Deoxys-D is a strong support Pokemon, but its lack of resistances makes it difficult to fit onto teams. This doesn't mean it isn't worth drafting, but it usually won't be the first choice for its role on a team.

Strong Wallbreakers: Deoxys-D is a great pivot to safely bring wallbreakers like Chi-Yu, Urshifu-S, and Roaring Moon onto the field. It also provides entry hazards to support their wallbreaking capabilities.

Spinblocker: Deoxys-D appreciates a teammate such as Gholdengo, Hisuian Zoroark, or Annihilape spinblocking to keep its entry hazards on the field.

Resistance Compression: Deoxys-D's great bulk is undermined by its lack of resistances, so these resistances need to be compensated for in the rest of the draft.

Dark-type Answers: All Deoxys-D sets are threatened by Dark-types, but its offensive setup sweeper sets are most affected, so Pokemon that threaten Dark-types like Iron Valiant, Quaquaval, and Galarian Zapdos are appreciated to enable its set versatility.

Checks and Counters

Disruption: Deoxys-D's main flaw is its passivity, which can be exploited by moves like Taunt, Encore, and Trick. This is more notable against faster threats, as it can use Taunt against slower ones.

Entry Hazards: If Deoxys-D is not using Heavy-Duty Boots, it is left vulnerable to all types of entry hazards, limiting its ability to act as a defensive wall.

Normal-types: Deoxys-D will commonly only have Night Shade as a significant damaging move, so Normal-types can take advantage of this so long as they don't mind a Knock Off or Thunder Wave.

Dark-types: Deoxys-D's low offenses make its offensive setup sets reliant on Stored Power, so Dark-types can effectively shut them down.
